Children are encouraged to interact and play with their family member during visits.

Our facilities include:

a soft play area

board games

activity bags available from the tea bar

A tea bar, operated by prisoners, offers drinks and snacks.

Staff are present throughout visits to help ensure everyone has a safe and enjoyable experience.

Although visitors are not routinely searched, searches may be required in certain circumstances to maintain safety and security.

Visitors who behave in a threatening or abusive manner may have their visit ended and may be asked to leave.

Additional support is available for women who do not receive visits.

Acorn House

Acorn House is a fully furnished family house that allows prisoners to spend extended daytime visits with family members or significant others.

This service is available in addition to regular prison visits.

Applications can be made through the Custodial Manager for MBU/Resettlement.

Each request is considered individually at the weekly Family team meeting.

Mother and Baby unit (MBU)

Women who are pregnant, or have a child under 18 months old, may be able to apply for a place in our Mother and Baby unit.

The unit is separate from the main prison and is located next to a nursery run by Action for Children.

Applications are considered individually and decisions are made based on the best interests of the child.

Key workers

Each prisoner is allocated a key worker.

Key workers support women to:

build confidence

make positive choices

work towards personal goals

access support and services

They meet regularly with prisoners, usually for around 1.5 hours every other week.

They work alongside other staff and organisations to support rehabilitation and personal development.

Strong relationships between staff and prisoners can help reduce self-harm, violence and other difficulties while promoting positive change.

Prison offender managers (POMs)

Every prisoner has a prison offender manager (POM).

Our POMs work with women throughout their sentence to:

support progression through their sentence plan

address risk factors

help prepare for release

They work closely with community offender managers to ensure plans are in place for housing, employment and other resettlement needs.

The level of contact is based on each person’s individual needs.

Pregnancy, mother and baby liaison officer (PMBLO)

The Pregnancy, mother and baby liaison officer (PMBLO) provides support and advice to women who:

are pregnant

have recently given birth

have experienced other pregnancy outcomes

are applying for or living in a mother and baby unit

have been separated from children under the age of 2

The PMBLO works with prison staff and external organisations to identify needs early, share information appropriately, and improve outcomes for mothers and their children.

Family engagement team

HMP Askham Grange works with the Prison Advice and Care Trust (PACT), which provides:

a full-time family engagement manager

a part-time family engagement worker

The PACT team supports both prisoners and families by:

helping families stay in touch

supporting family relationships

assisting with child-related issues

referring people to specialist services when needed

They can also help with communication with:

schools

social services

family courts

other relevant organisations

PACT runs workshops throughout the year, including:

Building Stronger Relationships

Preparing to Go Home

PACT is also the main point of contact for all matters relating to Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service (Cafcass).

For more information, visit the PACT website: HMP Askham Grange - Prison Advice and Care Trust

Storybook Mums

Women can record themselves reading a storybook for a child in their family.

The recording and book can then be sent to the child, helping maintain important family bonds while the parent is in prison.

This service is provided through the prison library.

Care leavers

People who have been in care may be entitled to support until they are 25 years old.

HMP Askham Grange recognises that care-experienced people may need additional support and works closely with local authorities and other organisations to help ensure they receive the services and opportunities they are entitled to.

Care leaver status is discussed during the induction process with a prison offender manager.

Support may include:

accessing rights and entitlements

information and advice

peer support groups

talks and workshops from care leaver organisations

We are committed to helping care-experienced women access the support they need to achieve positive outcomes both during custody and after release.

Safeguarding measures

Safeguarding

At HMP Askham Grange, we are committed to keeping people safe.

We have safeguarding procedures in place to protect women in our care, as well as vulnerable adults and children.

Everyone has the right to live free from abuse, harm, neglect, or exploitation. We take all safeguarding concerns seriously and have a responsibility to respond quickly and appropriately when concerns are raised.

If abuse is reported or suspected, action will be taken promptly in line with prison service policies and procedures.

We work closely with a range of organisations and professionals, including health, social care, and other partner agencies, to help ensure that women in our care are safe and receive the support they need.

Our staff work together to identify risks, respond to concerns, and promote the wellbeing of everyone in our care.

If you are worried about a loved one in prison you can:

Visit HMP Askham Grange - Prisoners’ Families Helpline for advice and contact details.

See our main Askham Grange Prison GOV.UK page for contact details, if you have a safeguarding concern.
